title: Optimized protocol for single-molecule RNA FISH to visualize gene expression in S. cerevisiae
protocol: Inoculate a single colony in 3 mL synthetic (complete or selective) yeast media.
Incubate tubes at 30°C in rotating wheel.
Measure the OD600 of the cultures.
Dilute yeast in 25 mL of SC media such that the cultures are at an OD600 of 0.5 the next morning.
Incubate the cultures in a 30°C orbital shaker at 200 rpm overnight.
Harvest each sample when the OD600 is 0.45–0.55 the next morning.
Cool tabletop centrifuge to 4°C and prepare two buckets of ice for the subsequent steps—one bucket for a bottle of buffer B and the other bucket for the samples.
Check OD600 of each sample and proceed with fixation when the OD600 is ∼0.5.
Let cultures grow until they reach an OD600 ∼0.5 before fixing them with formaldehyde.
Dilute cultures if the OD600 >0.6 to allow for recovery in 1-2 division cycles before fixation.
Add 4 mL of 32% PFA to a 50 mL falcon tube.
Add 21 mL of each yeast culture to the PFA to achieve a final concentration of 5% PFA.
Incubate samples at 18°C–22°C for 20 minutes, inverting the tubes every 5 minutes.
Spin the culture at 3000 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C and decant the media.
Quickly remove excess media by laying the 50 mL falcon tube upside down on tissues.
Carefully resuspend each pellet with 10 mL of ice-cold 1× buffer B.
Spin the culture at 3000 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C and decant the media.
Quickly remove excess media by laying the falcon tubes upside down on tissues.
Repeat the steps to resuspend each pellet in 10 mL of ice-cold 1× buffer B, spin, decant, and remove excess media two more times.
Dissolve the pellet in 1 mL of 1× buffer B after the third wash step.
Transfer the dissolved pellet to a 2 mL eppendorf tube.
Spin down cells at 845 × g for 3 min at 4°C.
Decant the media from the samples.
Resuspend each sample in 500 μL of spheroplasting buffer containing 300U of lyticase per sample.
Incubate samples in a 30°C thermoshaker for 5 min (100–300 rpm).
Spin samples for 4 min at 160 × g at 4°C.
Decant the spheroplasting buffer and gently wash the pellet once with 1 mL ice-cold 1× buffer B.
Spin at 160 × g at 4°C for 4 min.
Resuspend samples in 1 mL ice-cold 1× buffer B.
Gently pipet ∼400 μL of sample onto an 18 mm poly-L-lysine coated coverslips in a 12-well plate.
Incubate at 4°C for 30 min to let the cells adhere to the coverslips.
Wash the coverslip wells with ice-cold 1× buffer B.
Aspirate.
Add 2 mL of cold 70% ethanol to each well and incubate for at least one hour at -20°C before use.
Seal the plates with parafilm.
Incubate the sealed plates overnight at -20°C.
Thaw aliquots of hybridization buffer and probes at 18°C-22°C.
Prepare a petri dish for coverslips.
Label the base of the petri dish with sample names.
Cut circles of parafilm to fit inside a 10 cm petri dish.
Fold a kimwipe into a small square, dampen it with Milli-Q water.
Place the moistened kimwipe to the side of the dish to maintain humidity.
Aspirate ethanol from samples taken from -20°C.
Make a hybridization solution master mix for each sample using 52.8 μL of hybridization buffer and 2.2 μL of 2.5 μM probe.
Vortex well and store the hybridization solution at 18°C-22°C in the dark until use.
Rehydrate coverslips with 2 mL of wash buffer at 18°C–22°C.
Incubate rehydrated coverslips at 18°C–22°C for 5 minutes.
Pipette drops of approximately 50 μL of probe hybridization solution on the petri dish, on parafilm.
Remove coverslips from the 12-well plate with forceps and position them vertically to allow fluid accumulation at the base.
Tap off excess liquid gently without allowing the sample to dry completely.
Place cell side down onto the drop of probe mixture on the petri dish to avoid bubbles.
If bubbles are visible, tap the coverslip gently to remove them.
Seal the petri dish with parafilm and place in a humid 37°C incubator for 4 hours in the dark.
Place coverslips into 12-well plates with cell side up.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed 37°C wash buffer to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 30 min in the dark.
Aspirate the wash buffer from each well.
Add another 2 mL of pre-warmed 37°C wash buffer to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 30 min in the dark.
Thaw Prolong Gold with DAPI media at 18°C–22°C.
Make 2×SSC by diluting 20×SSC with Milli-Q water 10-fold.
Label microscope slides.
Aspirate the wash buffer from each well.
Rinse coverslips with 2×SSC by adding and aspirating the solution.
Add 2 mL of 1× PBS to each well.
Incubate for 5 min at 18°C–22°C, covering plate with foil.
Gently remove coverslips from the 12-well plate with forceps.
Position coverslips vertically to allow fluid to fall naturally.
Do not allow coverslips to air dry completely; cover with foil.
For an 18 mm coverslip, pipette 12–15 μL of Prolong Gold mounting media onto the microscope slide.
Pipette off any visible bubbles using a new tip.
Gently place coverslip face down on mounting media.
Place the slide in the dark once the sample is mounted.
Depress the plunger of the pipet to the first stop to dispense Prolong Gold onto the microscope slide.
Spin the Prolong Gold at 2000 × g for about 5 min before use.
Cover the mounted slides with foil.
Let the slides dry on a flat surface at 18°C–22°C for 24 hours before imaging.
Store the dried slides at −20°C for months if not imaged immediately.
Use an LED lamp (Lumencor SpectraX) or an alternative well-aligned light source such as a laser, mercury lamp, or metal-halide lamp.
Select excitation light with a narrow wavelength range of less than 30 nm for high specificity and reduced autofluorescence.
Choose a high numerical aperture (NA >= 1.3) objective to ensure optimal optical resolution.
Use an objective with a magnification between 50–65× for smFISH signal detection.
Select a final magnification that results in a pixel size of at least 100 nm on the camera chip.
Ensure the final magnification is appropriate, considering the importance of intensity information versus positional information for the research question.
Choose the correct excitation filters for each fluorophore based on their specific wavelengths.
Select narrow bandpass emission filters to prevent crosstalk between fluorophores.
Use 395/25 excitation filter for DAPI, 550/15 for Quasar570, and 640/30 for Quasar670.
Choose 460/50 emission filter for DAPI, 595/50 for Quasar570, and 697/60 for Quasar670.
Select dichroic mirrors: 350/550 for DAPI, 550/700 for Quasar570, and 550/800 for Quasar670.
Start imaging from the longest wavelength to prevent photobleaching of shorter wavelengths.
Use an sCMOS camera with a high dynamic range and small pixel size (6.5 μm) for imaging large areas.
Set the camera to use 1 × 1 binning for optimal resolution.
Utilize standard microscope software that allows tiling and z-stacks, such as MicroManager, for imaging.
If tiling is not possible in the software, manually image different positions on the coverslip.
Set acquisition conditions in imaging software for each smFISH signal using maximum power (100%).
Adjust exposure time between 250 ms and 1000 ms based on light source.
Use low power setting (20%) and very short exposure time for the DAPI channel.
Optimize exposure time to enhance spot detection while minimizing background noise and bleaching.
Acquire multiple z-slices with 300 nm steps, collecting at least 21 sections for diploid yeast imaging.
Image all z-sections in one channel before switching to another channel during acquisition.
Ensure consistent imaging conditions for slides from the same experiment.
